lessons.title: Practice Majority Vote Ensemble
lessons.description: Implement majority_vote(pred_lists) — each pred_lists[i] is predictions from one model. Tie → min label. The test checks that majority_vote([[1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1]]) equals [1, 1].
learning_objectives: This step takes the majority vote, using votes and 2.
lessons.starter_code:

    # TODO
    pass
lessons.solution_code:
from collections import Counter

def majority_vote(pred_lists):
    n = len(pred_lists[0])
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        votes = [plist[i] for plist in pred_lists]
        counts = Counter(votes)
        best = max(counts.values())
        out.append(min(v for v, c in counts.items() if c == best))
    return out

source.name: scikit-learn User Guide — Ensemble methods — 'combine the predictions of several base estimators'

lessons.title: Practice Checkpoint Tree Depth Limit
lessons.description: Implement should_stop(depth, max_depth, labels) True if depth>=max_depth or all labels equal. The test checks that should_stop(3, 3, [0, 1]) is true; should_stop(0, 5, [1, 1, 1]) is true; should_stop(1, 5, [0, 1]) is false.
learning_objectives: This step caps the depth at the limit, using depth and 3.
lessons.solution_code:
def should_stop(depth, max_depth, labels):
    return depth >= max_depth or len(set(labels)) <= 1

source.name: scikit-learn User Guide — Decision Trees — stopping criteria (depth, pure nodes)
